newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF awaits Ukraine budget before deciding new loan.
newsitem.headline: IMF awaits Ukraine budget before deciding new loan.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund will decide quickly whether to give Ukraine a new $2.5-3.0 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) once Ukraine passes its 1997 budget, the IMF's resident representative said on Wednesday.
"We usually try to move very fast. It's fairly quick," Alex Sundakov told Reuters.
Parliament is expected to debate the budget soon. President Leonid Kuchma has promised it would be passed by the end of March. By law it should have been passed by January 1.
Sundakov said the IMF and Ukraine have reached agreement on the budget package, which includes a series of new laws to reform the former Soviet republic's cumbersome taxation system.
"Once the package is passed, the fund will review what emerges from the process," Sundakov said.
Kuchma has said the deficit may be higher than the 5.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) -- four percent by Western calculations -- agreed with the IMF late last year.
The EFF would succeed an $867 million stand-by programme which expired this month.
"The main idea is the stand-by programme is in a sense short-term," Sundakov said. "The EFF has a whole different policy focus, to create conditions for growth."
